reason: CW14 par. 374 asserts 'the identification of the transformative substance with God'; transformative substance = arcane substance, and grounding 'God' as god-image is the correct psychological referent since Jung explicitly frames the theologem as a projection of the collective unconscious in this same paragraph.

CW14 par. 372: the aqua permanens ('the arcane substance par excellence') is what the alchemists had in mind as an all-pervading essence, and Jung states 'there is probably no more suitable psychological concept for this than the collective unconscious'. Quote exact; direction correct.

CW14 par. 372 says the collective unconscious is that 'whose nucleus and ordering “principle” is the self'. Subject/object direction matches: the self is the nucleus and ordering principle of the collective unconscious.
CW14 par. 381 says verbatim 'Dissolution is the prerequisite for redemption'; the object is redemption (and figurative death for transformation), not rebirth, which the paragraph never asserts.

CW14 par. 388 says psychic disunity 'becomes the “vir unus,” the unified man' in the albedo, but this is explicitly only the completion of 'the first part' of the work; equating it with 'the whole man' (homo totus, goal of the entire opus) is identity overreach.

CW14 par. 403 says the water and containing vessel 'always signify the mother, the feminine principle best characterized by yin'; the paragraph asserts the mother / feminine principle, not the Great Mother archetype specifically.

CW14 par. 410 states verbatim 'Undoubtedly the hierosgamos of the substances is a projection of unconscious contents'. Direction and referents correct; the paragraph's later qualification concerns where those contents reside, not the projection claim itself.
CW14 par. 415 states verbatim 'She characterizes the arcane substance in its initial, “chaotic,” maternal state', with 'she' being the meretrix (whore) named in the preceding sentence.
CW14 par. 416 states 'Venus appears as the feminine aspect of the king, or as we should say, his anima'. Subject, object, and direction all match.

CW14 par. 424: the uroboros mythologem is 'translated into feminine form' as 'the mother who merges with her own substance, “eating her own tail”'; the Cantilena's mother is the queen ('The queen is in a condition of psychic pregnancy'), so regina enacting the ouroboros is supported.
CW14 par. 424 states verbatim 'the anima has become activated and sends her contents into consciousness'. Exact match in subject, relation, object, and direction.

CW14 par. 425: as the dogmatic view lost force and 'the fascination of dogma began to pall', 'there grew up in their unconscious the compensating image of the king's renewal' — the king's renewal compensates the fading of dogma, direction correct.

CW12 par. 346 states verbatim that 'the real root of alchemy is to be sought less in philosophical doctrines than in the projections of individual investigators'. Direction correct: alchemy is rooted in projection.

CW12 par. 376 asserts 'an unconscious identity between the psyche of the alchemist and the arcane substance'; the relation's 'unconsciously-identical' correctly carries the psychic register, and artifex = alchemist.

CW12 par. 378 asserts 'the stone is man' and 'the identity of something in man with something concealed in matter'; 'inner-man' is a specific term the paragraph never uses, so the object over-specifies the referent.

CW12 par. 383 says the 'darknesses of our mind' coincide with the nigredo, i.e. the author experiences the initial stage as identical with his own psychic condition; 'unconsciousness' as a concept is not asserted — the coincidence is with the alchemist's dark psychic state.

CW12 par. 400: the opus was 'a question of actualizing those contents of the unconscious which are outside nature... and therefore an a priori of archetypal character' — the opus actualizes archetypal contents/images; direction correct.

CW12 par. 404 describes Mercurius as 'poison and yet healing draught—a symbol uniting all opposites', preceded by a chain of paired opposites he unites (matter/spirit, cold/fiery). Exact quote; direction correct.

CW12 par. 404: 'When the alchemist speaks of Mercurius... inwardly he means the world-creating spirit concealed or imprisoned in matter' — the world spirit in matter, correctly grounded as spiritus mundi; 'inwardly-signifies' matches the outer/inner contrast in the text.

CW12 par. 413 states that as 'the Godhead conceals itself in the man of low degree, so in the “philosophy” it hides in the uncomely stone'; god-image hides in the lapis, direction correct, and the paragraph frames this as projection, matching the god-image referent.

CW12 par. 420: the alchemist's attention 'is not directed to his own salvation through God's grace, but to the liberation of God from the darkness of matter' — the artifex seeks the liberation of the deity lost in matter; subject, object, and direction correct.
